source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 15: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
\(\sqrt{x}\) do jagah hai: \(\tan^{-1}\) ke andar aur denominator mein. Aisi soorat mein \(t = \sqrt{x}\) rakhna faidemand hai.
\(dt = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), yani \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\); denominator khud ba khud khatam!
Phir \(2\int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\) bachta hai, jo Question 11 wala hi kaam hai.
Plan: substitution, parts (\(\tan^{-1}t \cdot 1\)), log integral, wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(t = \sqrt{x}\) rakhenge; phir \(2\int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\) parts se.

Substitution
\[t = \sqrt{x} \Rightarrow dt = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx\]
\[\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\]
\[= 2\int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x}\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) hai, is liye \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}}\) seedha \(2\,dt\) ban gaya.

Log wala integral
\[= 2t\tan^{-1}t - 2\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+t^2) + c\]
\[= 2t\tan^{-1}t - \ln(1+t^2) + c\]
Kyun: \(2t\) denominator \(1 + t^2\) ka derivative hai, is liye \(\frac{1}{2}\) laga kar log; bahar ka 2 aur yeh \(\frac{1}{2}\) cancel.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[= 2\sqrt{x}\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x} - \ln(1 + x) + c\]
Kyun: \(t = \sqrt{x}\) aur \(t^2 = x\).
Dhyan dein: \(1 + t^2\) ko \(1 + \sqrt{x}\) mat likhiye; \(t^2 = x\) hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ldots) = \dfrac{\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}} + \dfrac{1}{1+x} - \dfrac{1}{1+x}\]
Kyun: \(2\sqrt{x}\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\), aur \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\) ka derivative chain rule se \(\frac{1}{1+x}\cdot\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\). \(\frac{1}{1+x}\) cancel ho kar integrand bacha.
